# Third-party notices

The root LICENSE is the repository owner's existing AGPL-3.0 text and has not been replaced. This directory does not relicense dependencies.

- `python-inventory.json` records distributions actually present in the tested application image (including base Python packaging tools). `python/` preserves their installed license/author/notice texts, including bundled vendor notices where supplied by the distribution.
- Runtime versions/hashes are in `requirements/u1-runtime.txt`; the Docker build downloads them directly from the package index. In particular psycopg 3.3.9 is LGPL-3.0-only, regex carries Apache-2.0 AND CNRI-Python, Django/asgiref are BSD, Gunicorn is MIT, unicodedata2 carries Apache-2.0, and typing-extensions carries PSF terms. Consult the actual notices, not only this short list.
- Psycopg is used as an unmodified dynamically imported Python package. Its exact source distribution is available at https://pypi.org/project/psycopg/3.3.9/#files and upstream https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg/tree/3.3.9 ; the pinned package requirements and Dockerfile permit rebuilding/replacing it. No binary images are published by this repository's installer work. If redistributing built images, preserve notices and supply corresponding library/application source and installation/relinking information as required by the applicable licenses; a URL alone is not a universal binary redistribution compliance procedure.
- Embedded Unicode data notices remain at `researchloop/cards/unicode17/LICENSE.txt` and `researchloop/static/u2/unicode17/LICENSE.txt`; provenance manifests remain with the data. Do not remove them.
- Optional browser QA dependencies in `package-lock.json` include Playwright (Apache-2.0), axe-core integrations (see their package notices), and Lighthouse (Apache-2.0). They are fetched into the optional QA image, not bundled with app source. npm package notices and Playwright browser/image notices remain in their distributions. Browser/platform binaries are not committed here.
- Python/PostgreSQL/Linux base images retain their upstream operating-system package notices in the images (including `/usr/share/doc` where provided). This source-only repository does not claim to replace their license inventories. Review binary-image distribution obligations separately before publishing images.
